articles.title: Race progress update: refueling!
articles.excerpt: After 48 hours of racing, bodies are tired but minds are working at full speed as it's already time for the first strategic decisions to determine the opportune moment to turn south. Between meals and naps, a midday update on the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe fleet.

articles.title: BREAKING NEWS - Fabien Delahaye, aboard LEGALLAIS, abandons the race due to an ankle injury
articles.excerpt: This morning around 6 a.m., while sailing in 25 knots of wind and very rough seas, Fabien Delahaye injured his ankle while going to lower his spinnaker on the foredeck of his Class40. Since then, the skipper of LEGALLAIS, who is sailing for the fourth season under the colors of the Normandy-based company, has been in contact with the race doctor. The pain is extremely intense, and he is unable to put any weight on his foot.

articles.title: the first light with the sailors 🌊
articles.excerpt: Après une nouvelle nuit d'engagement total, les premières lueurs de l'aube éclairent les cockpits. Entre veille météo, réglages millimétrés et manœuvres, les skippers partagent un aperçu de leur quotidien au large.

articles.title: 🌦️ WEATHER BULLETIN OF NOVEMBER 3
articles.excerpt: Ce mardi 3 novembre, 2 jours après le départ de la Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe 2026, un puissant anticyclone reste centré sur le nord des Iles Britanniques et intéresse encore une grande partie de la flotte mais un front perturbé concerne les marins les plus à l’ouest.

articles.title: BREAKING NEWS - Rudder damage on the IMOCA Les P’tits Doudous
articles.excerpt: During the night, Armel contacted his team after encountering damage to one of his two rudders.

articles.title: Living on the edge...and falling off!
articles.excerpt: Major damage has been reported to the port-side foil of the Maxi Edmond de Rothschild: Charles Caudrelier is safe and is currently working to secure his boat. After capsizing his ORMA 60 Francis Joyon safe on cargo ship heading for Ireland where he should arrive soon.

articles.title: BREAKING NEWS - Foil damage aboard the Maxi Edmond de Rothschild
articles.excerpt: This Tuesday morning, shortly before 5 a.m., Charles Caudrelier alerted his shore team to damage to the port foil of the Maxi Edmond de Rothschild.

articles.title: BREAKING NEWS - Francis Joyon (Oceans) safe aboard a cargo ship
articles.excerpt: After his boat capsized on Monday, November 2nd, around 3 p.m., Francis Joyon was rescued by the cargo ship Maersk Columbus at 11 p.m. The skipper of the Vintage Multi Oceans is doing well and is currently en route to Ireland where he will disembark in the coming hours.

articles.title: BREAKING NEWS - Francis Joyon (Oceans) has capsized
articles.excerpt: Francis Joyon s’est retourné à bord de son ORMA Océans. D’après les premiers éléments fournis le skipper confirme qu’il n’est pas blessé. Une opération de secours, en concertation avec la direction de course, a été déclenchée avec le CROSS* de Jobourg et les autorités britanniques.

articles.title: 📸 View from onboard: second afternoon of racing
Crown duels. Head-to-heads increase the pace.
articles.excerpt: The leaders of the Route du Rhum Destination Guadeloupe, the Ultim giants of the ocean, were making the best of the fast conditions as they sprint westwards on the second day of racing since leaving Saint-Malo in beautiful sunshine and modest breezes Sunday lunchtime.

articles.title: 📸 Day 1: Photos from the edge
articles.excerpt: Twenty-four hours have already passed since the start! After an intense first day of sailing and a night battling the elements, our skippers are finally sharing their first moments on the open sea. Between intense concentration, choppy seas, and the first sunrises, dive into the heart of the action with these very first images sent from onboard.

articles.title: 🎥 The first onboard images from the skippers
articles.excerpt: Join the skippers on board after 24 hours of racing and the first night at sea.

articles.title: Technical stopover for Marco Guerra
articles.excerpt: This morning at 9:20 AM, Marco Guerra, skipper of the Class40 #207 IMAGIN'ACT–SOCOMEC, contacted his technical team. He is currently experiencing problems with his keel, a leak, and electronics. The decision has been made to make a technical stopover in Port La-Forêt. Since leaving Saint-Malo, Marco has been experiencing electronic problems that he hasn't been able to resolve. And this morning, he noticed unusual movements on the keel. articles.title: NEWS FLASH: Dismasting of Class40 n°205 skippered by Quentin Le Nabour
articles.excerpt: Less than 24 hours after the start of the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe, given on Sunday, November 1st at 1:02 pm, the Class40 n°205, skippered by Quentin Le Nabour, dismasted.
